papers.title: ProQuant: Preserving Expert Quality over Quantity in Ultra-Low-Bit Quantization of Mixture-of-Experts Models
papers.abstract_en: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) large language models reduce computation through sparse activation but still incur substantial storage costs. Mixed-precision post-training quantization (PTQ) reduces these costs by quantizing different model components at different bit widths, but existing methods often struggle to preserve generation quality under tight bit budgets. We identify two key challenges: (1) nonlinear quantization errors at extremely low precision are underestimated when cross-layer propagation is ignored; (2) direct router fine-tuning may cause routing drift, and calibration gains may not generalize to downstream tasks. To address these issues, we propose ProQuant, a weight-only PTQ framework for MoE models. Prune-or-Prioritize Mixed-Precision Allocation (PoP) jointly optimizes expert pruning and bit-width assignment. It allows higher-precision experts to substitute for severely degraded ones while improving bit-budget utilization. Routing-Consistent RMSNorm Finetune (RoCo) adapts expert input representations through mathematically equivalent transformations. It compensates for quantization errors to reduce routing drift. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ProQuant outperforms existing methods across diverse generative tasks. Code is available at https://github.com/ThrowBug/ProQuant.git.
papers.abstract_zh: 混合专家（MoE）大语言模型通过稀疏激活降低计算量，但仍带来可观的存储开销。混合精度训练后量化（PTQ）通过以不同位宽量化不同模型组件来降低这些开销，但现有方法在紧张的比特预算下往往难以保持生成质量。我们识别出两个关键挑战：（1）当忽略跨层传播时，极低精度下的非线性量化误差会被低估；（2）直接微调路由器可能导致路由漂移，且校准收益可能无法泛化到下游任务。为解决这些问题，我们提出 ProQuant，一个面向 MoE 模型的仅权重量化 PTQ 框架。Prune-or-Prioritize 混合精度分配（PoP）联合优化专家剪枝与位宽分配，允许更高精度的专家替代严重退化的专家，同时提升比特预算利用率。Routing-Consistent RMSNorm Finetune（RoCo）通过数学等价变换调整专家输入表示，以补偿量化误差、减少路由漂移。大量实验表明，ProQuant 在多种生成任务上优于现有方法。代码见 https://github.com/ThrowBug/ProQuant.git。
papers.tldr_zh: ProQuant 提出联合优化专家剪枝与位宽分配的 PoP 以及通过数学等价变换微调 RMSNorm 的 RoCo，以在超低位宽下保持 MoE 模型的生成质量。
why_it_matters: 匹配 LLM：large language model, language model
匹配 预训练 / 后训练：post-training
evidence: 实验或理论证据信号：extensive experiment
开放资源信号：code is available

papers.title: VisualEvolve: A Skill Self-Evolution Framework for Visual Reasoning
papers.abstract_en: Visual tool use enables vision-language models (VLMs) to acquire task-relevant evidence, but its effectiveness can be limited by predefined visual operations and the tool-use strategies learned during training. Representing these operations and strategies as reusable external skills allows them to be refined through self-evolution without updating model parameters. However, skill refinement can introduce performance regressions. Meanwhile, inspecting accumulated task execution trajectories together with skill evolution history may lead to evolution evidence overload. To address these challenges, we propose VisualEvolve, a self-evolving framework that evolves executable visual operations and tool-use strategies for VLMs through a Select--Execute--Evolve--Evaluate cycle. Skill-Library Snapshot Selection uses performance on a fixed validation set disjoint from execution tasks to select an effective historical snapshot for subsequent evolution, limiting the propagation of performance regressions. Progressive Evidence Access (PEA) guides capability-gap diagnosis through a coarse-to-fine hierarchy comprising the Skill-Performance Report, Evolution Log, Trajectory Summaries, and relevant raw trajectory segments. Across four VLM backbones and six evaluation sets from three benchmarks, VisualEvolve improves over the Initial Skill Library in 23 of 24 settings, with a maximum gain of 15.1 percentage points on VisualProbe Hard using Qwen3.5-Plus. Ablation studies support the contributions of Snapshot Selection and PEA, while further experiments show that skills can be improved using experience from different data settings and directly reused across backbones. Moreover, VisualEvolve enables effective skill self-evolution with over an order of magnitude fewer task-solving trajectories than estimated for representative RL-based methods.
papers.abstract_zh: 视觉工具使用使视觉语言模型（VLM）能够获取与任务相关的证据，但其有效性可能受限于预定义的视觉操作和训练期间学到的工具使用策略。将这些操作和策略表示为可复用的外部技能，使其能够通过自我进化进行改进，而无需更新模型参数。然而，技能改进可能引入性能回退。同时，检查累积的任务执行轨迹以及技能进化历史可能导致进化证据过载。为应对这些挑战，我们提出 VisualEvolve，一个自我进化框架，通过“选择—执行—进化—评估”循环为 VLM 进化可执行的视觉操作和工具使用策略。技能库快照选择利用在与执行任务不相交的固定验证集上的表现，为后续进化选择一个有效的历史快照，从而限制性能回退的传播。渐进式证据访问（PEA）通过由技能-性能报告、进化日志、轨迹摘要和相关原始轨迹片段组成的由粗到细的层级结构，引导能力差距诊断。在四个 VLM 骨干模型和来自三个基准的六个评估集上，VisualEvolve 在 24 个设置中的 23 个上优于初始技能库，在使用 Qwen3.5-Plus 的 VisualProbe Hard 上最大提升为 15.1 个百分点。消融研究支持快照选择和 PEA 的贡献，进一步实验表明技能可以利用不同数据设置的经验进行改进，并可直接跨骨干模型复用。此外，VisualEvolve 能够以比代表性 RL 方法估计所需少一个数量级以上的任务求解轨迹实现有效的技能自我进化。
papers.tldr_zh: VisualEvolve 通过“选择—执行—进化—评估”循环及快照选择与渐进式证据访问，在不更新参数的情况下进化 VLM 的视觉操作与工具使用技能，在 24 个设置中的 23 个上优于初始技能库。
why_it_matters: 匹配 MLLM / VLM：vision-language model, vlm
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Agentic Ensemble with Vision-Language Models for Visual Anomaly Detection
papers.abstract_en: Visual anomaly detection aims to detect abnormal objects, while anomaly samples are often scarce during model training. Assembling multiple pretrained detectors can help by leveraging their transferable image scores and anomaly maps. However, most existing ensemble methods apply fixed fusion rules over saved predictions which struggle when pretrained detectors clearly disagree due to different training objectives, priors, and visual representations. To this end, we design AnomalyAgent, a post-training fusion framework for accurate visual anomaly detection. AnomalyAgent aligns heterogeneous scores and maps, summarizes score- and region-level disagreement, and treats fusion as a finite action-selection problem. It implements two types of actions: 1) score actions that determine how to fuse image-level detector confidence via consensus, robust aggregation, detector weighting, or score-map consistency; 2) map actions that fuse dense anomaly responses via consensus, detector weighting, geometric aggregation, or disagreement correction. A constrained vision-language model (VLM) is introduced to inspect high-conflict samples and select valid score action and map action to produce the final prediction. We evaluate AnomalyAgent on MVTec AD and VisA as primary benchmarks, together with seven additional public anomaly benchmarks and Real-IAD for large-scale score-level evaluation. Across these benchmarks, AnomalyAgent consistently improves over equal-weight fusion and achieves the best mean image AUROC and pixel AP among the compared fusion methods on MVTec AD and VisA, while demonstrating robust transfer across additional anomaly domains.
papers.abstract_zh: 视觉异常检测旨在检测异常对象，而异常样本在模型训练期间往往稀缺。集成多个预训练检测器可以通过利用其可迁移的图像分数和异常图提供帮助。然而，大多数现有集成方法对保存的预测应用固定融合规则，当预训练检测器因不同的训练目标、先验和视觉表示而明显不一致时，这些方法难以应对。为此，我们设计 AnomalyAgent，一个用于准确视觉异常检测的后训练融合框架。AnomalyAgent 对齐异构分数和图，总结分数级与区域级分歧，并将融合视为有限动作选择问题。它实现两类动作：1）分数动作，通过共识、稳健聚合、检测器加权或分数-图一致性决定如何融合图像级检测器置信度；2）图动作，通过共识、检测器加权、几何聚合或分歧校正融合稠密异常响应。引入受约束的视觉语言模型（VLM）检查高冲突样本，并选择有效的分数动作和图动作以产生最终预测。我们在 MVTec AD 和 VisA 作为主要基准，以及七个额外公开异常基准和 Real-IAD 用于大规模分数级评估上评估 AnomalyAgent。在这些基准上，AnomalyAgent 一致优于等权融合，并在 MVTec AD 和 VisA 上在所比较的融合方法中取得最佳平均图像 AUROC 和像素 AP，同时在额外异常领域展现出稳健迁移。
papers.tldr_zh: AnomalyAgent 将多检测器异常检测融合建模为有限动作选择，由受约束 VLM 在高冲突样本上选择分数动作与图动作，在 MVTec AD 和 VisA 上取得最佳平均图像 AUROC 与像素 AP。
why_it_matters: 匹配 MLLM / VLM：vision-language model, vlm
匹配 预训练 / 后训练：post-training
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: IQuest-Q1: Advancing Foundation Capabilities for Agentic CLI Systems
papers.abstract_en: We present IQuest-Q1, a sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) agentic foundation model with 320B total parameters (15B activated). IQuest-Q1 is developed through a three-stage process: (1) stable and efficient pre-training, combining Stable SplitNorm, Muon, and muP with a two-stage curriculum whose second stage increases the coding-data mixture, preserving a wide stability margin between safe and optimal learning rates; (2) fine-grained mid-training, expanding the data mixture across domains and formats and progressively extending the context; and (3) multi-scaffold with multi-version post-training, combining SFT, domain-specialized RL, and MOPD across various scaffolds to integrate complementary training signals and strengthen agentic coding capabilities. Furthermore, model merging combines different experts and checkpoints from different stages while mitigating conflicts among their parameter updates. The resulting IQuest-Q1 demonstrates capabilities in both coding and general tasks. We release IQuest-Q1 as an open-source model to support community research and development.
papers.abstract_zh: 我们提出 IQuest-Q1，一个稀疏混合专家（MoE）智能体基础模型，总参数 320B（激活 15B）。IQuest-Q1 通过三阶段流程开发：（1）稳定高效的预训练，结合 Stable SplitNorm、Muon 和 muP，并采用两阶段课程，其第二阶段提高代码数据混合比例，在安全学习率与最优学习率之间保持较宽的稳定裕度；（2）细粒度中期训练，跨领域和格式扩展数据混合并逐步延长上下文；（3）多脚手架与多版本后训练，在各种脚手架下结合 SFT、领域专用 RL 和 MOPD，以整合互补的训练信号并增强智能体编码能力。此外，模型合并结合不同专家以及不同阶段的检查点，同时缓解其参数更新之间的冲突。所得 IQuest-Q1 在编码和通用任务上均展现出能力。我们以开源模型形式发布 IQuest-Q1，以支持社区研究与开发。
papers.tldr_zh: IQuest-Q1 是一个 320B 总参数、15B 激活的稀疏 MoE 智能体基础模型，经预训练、中期训练和多脚手架后训练三阶段构建，并开源发布。
why_it_matters: 匹配 预训练 / 后训练：pre-training, post-training

papers.title: A Strong MoE Is All You Need for Process Supervision
papers.abstract_en: Process reward models (PRMs) provide fine-grained supervision for multi-step reasoning, yet obtaining reliable process labels remains a central bottleneck. Existing approaches typically rely on human annotation, rollout-based estimation, or auxiliary verification. In this work, we explore a different source of process supervision natively exposed by Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models: expert routing. We show that simple routing statistics provide an intrinsic process-confidence signal that is competitive with conventional output-logit confidence. Building on this observation, we construct routing confidence by combining overall routing mass, head routing mass, and within-step routing variation, and introduce RoCo-Rethink, which identifies the least confident reasoning step and selectively regenerates the subsequent trajectory. We further introduce RoCo-PRM, which uses a strong MoE to automatically annotate reasoning trajectories with routing-derived step scores and distills them into a standalone PRM. Across multiple MoE architectures and diverse reasoning tasks, both RoCo-Rethink and RoCo-PRM consistently outperform strong baselines, while RoCo-PRM transfers effectively across both model architectures and tasks. Our findings suggest that expert routing is more than a computational dispatch mechanism: it provides an architecture-native source of process supervision for reasoning.
papers.abstract_zh: 过程奖励模型（PRM）为多步推理提供细粒度监督，但获取可靠的过程标签仍是核心瓶颈。现有方法通常依赖人工标注、基于采样的估计或辅助验证。在本工作中，我们探索了混合专家（MoE）模型原生暴露的另一种过程监督来源：专家路由。我们表明，简单的路由统计量提供了一种内在的过程置信度信号，其效果可与传统的输出 logit 置信度相竞争。基于这一观察，我们通过组合整体路由质量、头路由质量以及步内路由变化来构建路由置信度，并提出 RoCo-Rethink，它识别置信度最低的推理步骤，并选择性地重新生成后续轨迹。我们进一步提出 RoCo-PRM，它使用强 MoE 模型自动为推理轨迹标注由路由推导的步骤分数，并将其蒸馏到一个独立的 PRM 中。在多种 MoE 架构和多样化的推理任务上，RoCo-Rethink 和 RoCo-PRM 均持续优于强基线，同时 RoCo-PRM 能有效地跨模型架构和任务迁移。我们的发现表明，专家路由不仅仅是一种计算调度机制：它为推理提供了一种架构原生的过程监督来源。
papers.tldr_zh: 利用 MoE 专家路由统计量构建过程置信度信号，提出 RoCo-Rethink 重生成低置信步骤与 RoCo-PRM 蒸馏独立过程奖励模型，在多种 MoE 架构和推理任务上优于强基线。

evidence: 实验或理论证据信号：strong baseline

papers.title: A Multi-Agent Framework for Automated Machine Learning with Evidence-based Planning for Medical Image Analysis
papers.abstract_en: Deep learning has become the default tool for medical image analysis, driven by the open-source movement. However, achieving the best performance on a given task remains difficult, with architecture selection and hyperparameter optimization (HPO) still considered "more of an art than a science". Automated machine learning (AutoML) automates parts of model training, yet helps little in medical imaging: general-purpose approaches lack medical architectures and preprocessing, and medical-focused ones demand engineering expertise and remain confined to narrow tasks such as 3D segmentation. We introduce MedicalMLOmni, a multi-agent AutoML framework that automates model training for diverse single- and multi-modal medical tasks through a natural language interface. Specifically, MedicalMLOmni performs evidence-based planning by retrieving published results to guide model selection and configuration, and employs parallel HPO where multiple agents explore adjustment strategies concurrently. MedicalMLOmni achieves the best score on 19 of 20 benchmarks; PMC-VQA is the exception, where a vision-language model with broader pre-training leads. Backbone-matched controls attribute the gains to the framework, not the backbone. By removing coding requirements, MedicalMLOmni lowers the barrier for domain experts with rich datasets but limited engineering expertise.
papers.abstract_zh: 在开源运动的推动下，深度学习已成为医学图像分析的默认工具。然而，在给定任务上取得最佳性能仍然困难，架构选择和超参数优化（HPO）仍被视为“更像艺术而非科学”。自动化机器学习（AutoML）自动化了部分模型训练，但对医学影像帮助有限：通用方法缺乏医学架构和预处理，而面向医学的方法需要工程专业知识，且局限于 3D 分割等狭窄任务。我们提出 MedicalMLOmni，一个多智能体 AutoML 框架，通过自然语言接口为多样化的单模态和多模态医学任务自动化模型训练。具体而言，MedicalMLOmni 通过检索已发表结果来指导模型选择和配置，执行基于证据的规划，并采用并行 HPO，其中多个智能体同时探索调整策略。MedicalMLOmni 在 20 个基准中的 19 个上取得最佳分数；PMC-VQA 是例外，在该基准上具有更广泛预训练的视觉语言模型领先。骨干匹配的对照实验将增益归因于框架而非骨干。通过消除编码要求，MedicalMLOmni 降低了拥有丰富数据集但工程专业知识有限领域专家的门槛。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出多智能体 AutoML 框架 MedicalMLOmni，通过检索已发表结果进行基于证据的规划并采用多智能体并行超参数优化，在 20 个医学基准中的 19 个上取得最佳分数。
why_it_matters: 匹配 预训练 / 后训练：pre-training

papers.title: MoEZip: Routing-Aware KV Cache Compression for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts LLMs
papers.abstract_en: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models scale model capacity efficiently by activating a small subset of parameters per token. However, in long-context inference, memory remains a major bottleneck because the KV cache grows linearly with sequence length. Existing KV cache compression methods reduce this cost for dense transformers, but overlook a problem specific to MoE: KV eviction can change which experts are selected during answer generation, degrading the generation quality. We propose MoEZip, a routing-aware KV cache compression for sparse MoE language models. To estimate the sensitivity of expert routing to perturbation, we propose a novel metric based on the Fisher information matrix of routing distributions. MoEZip combines this metric with attention weights for routing-aware scoring of contexts. Finally, we compose a complementary scoring system that combines eviction methods for dense and sparse-MoE architectures. Experiments show that MoEZip achieves robust performance under aggressive cache compression on various benchmarks. At a KV retention ratio of 10\%, MoEZip improves over the SoTA baseline by +24 and +20 points on average on LongBench and RULER, corresponding to 2.3$\times$ and 4.9$\times$ higher scores, respectively.
papers.abstract_zh: 混合专家（MoE）语言模型通过为每个 token 激活一小部分参数来高效扩展模型容量。然而，在长上下文推理中，内存仍是主要瓶颈，因为 KV 缓存随序列长度线性增长。现有 KV 缓存压缩方法降低了稠密 Transformer 的这一开销，但忽略了 MoE 特有的问题：KV 驱逐可能改变答案生成过程中被选中的专家，从而降低生成质量。我们提出 MoEZip，一种面向稀疏 MoE 语言模型的路由感知 KV 缓存压缩方法。为估计专家路由对扰动的敏感度，我们提出一种基于路由分布 Fisher 信息矩阵的新度量。MoEZip 将该度量与注意力权重结合，对上下文进行路由感知评分。最后，我们构建一个互补的评分系统，结合面向稠密和稀疏 MoE 架构的驱逐方法。实验表明，MoEZip 在多种基准上于激进缓存压缩下取得稳健性能。在 KV 保留率为 10% 时，MoEZip 在 LongBench 和 RULER 上平均比 SoTA 基线分别提升 +24 和 +20 分，对应分数分别高出 2.3 倍和 4.9 倍。
papers.tldr_zh: MoEZip 提出基于路由分布 Fisher 信息矩阵的路由感知评分并与注意力权重结合，在 10% KV 保留率下显著优于基线。
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: P$^3$-VLM: A Point-based Alternative for Grounded 3D Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Examining existing benchmarks for grounding in 3D VLMs reveals a pervasive "semantic leakage" in the evaluation and prompting protocols: a heavy reliance on bounding boxes as spatial prompts or representation primitives. Because bounding boxes are highly informative of object categories, they introduce a shortcut for the models to neglect visual information during 3D VLM training. We demonstrate this with a "blind" LLM that, prompted only with the box coordinates, can perform surprisingly well. To further analyze this shortcut, we propose point-based grounding prompting - querying models with a single 3D point instead of a box. Under this protocol, the accuracy of the blind LLM drops from 36.4% to 18.0% on ScanNet's Nr3D, and similarly degrades for 3D VLMs (e.g. LL3DA). Building on this insight, we introduce P$^3$-VLM, a novel tri-pathway 3D VLM that supports point-based prompts and achieves 52.1% state-of-the-art accuracy on location-grounded captioning under this setting. To achieve this, we redesign the architecture while keeping it detector-free, scene-centric, and suitable for 3D GS inputs. P$^3$-VLM utilizes three complementary pathways (location-, task-, and context-aware), enabling strong reasoning about scenes without any bounding box dependencies. The key benefit of point-based learning is a consistent improvement across settings: P$^3$-VLM achieves state-of-the-art performance under point-based grounding while also improving robustness, OOD generalization, and performance on ungrounded scene-centric 3D VQA benchmarks, reflecting its reduced reliance on bounding-box shortcuts and resulting stronger visual-spatial reasoning.
papers.abstract_zh: 考察现有的 3D VLM 定位基准可以发现，评估与提示协议中普遍存在“语义泄漏”：严重依赖边界框作为空间提示或表示基元。由于边界框高度蕴含物体类别信息，它们为模型在 3D VLM 训练中忽视视觉信息提供了捷径。我们用一个“盲”LLM 证明了这一点：仅向它提供框坐标作为提示，它就能取得出奇好的表现。为进一步分析这一捷径，我们提出基于点的定位提示——用单个 3D 点而非边界框来查询模型。在该协议下，盲 LLM 在 ScanNet 的 Nr3D 上的准确率从 36.4% 降至 18.0%，3D VLM（如 LL3DA）也出现类似下降。基于这一发现，我们提出 P$^3$-VLM，一种新颖的三通路 3D VLM，支持基于点的提示，并在该设置下的位置定位描述任务上取得 52.1% 的最先进准确率。为此，我们重新设计了架构，同时保持其无检测器、以场景为中心，并适用于 3D GS 输入。P$^3$-VLM 利用三条互补通路（位置感知、任务感知和上下文感知），在无任何边界框依赖的情况下实现对场景的强推理。基于点学习的关键优势是在各种设置下带来一致提升：P$^3$-VLM 在基于点的定位下取得最先进性能，同时提升了鲁棒性、OOD 泛化能力，以及在非定位、以场景为中心的 3D VQA 基准上的表现，这反映出其对边界框捷径的依赖减少，并由此获得更强的视觉-空间推理能力。
papers.tldr_zh: 论文指出 3D VLM 定位评估中边界框提示造成语义泄漏，提出用单点提示的 P$^3$-VLM 三通路架构，在 ScanNet Nr3D 等设置下取得最先进定位描述准确率并提升鲁棒性与 OOD 泛化。
why_it_matters: 匹配 MLLM / VLM：vision-language model, vlm
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: LocalAgent: Collaborative Agentic Verification for Fine-Grained Instance-Level Consistency
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have made rapid progress in general visual understanding, yet they still struggle with fine-grained instance-level consistency verification, where the goal is to determine whether two images depict the exact same physical object under varying viewpoints, illumination, and backgrounds. This task requires both global semantic perception and precise examination of subtle local evidence, since semantically similar objects may differ only in small suspicious regions. To address this challenge, we propose LocalAgent, a collaborative agentic framework that integrates the complementary strengths of a generalist MLLM and lightweight specialist verifiers. The MLLM first reasons globally to identify suspicious local regions, which are then delegated to a Local Evidence Verifier (LEV) toolkit for fine-grained appearance and geometric matching. LEV comprises Local Appearance Consistency (LAC), which estimates appearance similarity under illumination and color changes, and Local Geometric Correspondence (LGC), which estimates spatial correspondence under viewpoint changes. LEV returns structured scalar evidence that the MLLM integrates for the final decision. We further introduce an auxiliary-capped reinforcement fine-tuning (RFT) strategy, in which answer correctness dominates auxiliary tool-use and format signals, enabling the policy to learn when verification is necessary. Experiments show that LocalAgent improves mean accuracy by 4.9% over the strongest CoT-RFT baseline while invoking a verifier on only 12.13% of samples and preserving the general multimodal capabilities of the underlying MLLM. The open-source repository is available at https://github.com/Firefly-zoo/LocalAgent-main.
papers.abstract_zh: 多模态大语言模型（MLLM）在通用视觉理解方面取得了快速进展，但在细粒度实例级一致性验证上仍存在困难，该任务的目标是判断两张图像在不同视角、光照和背景下是否描绘了完全相同的物理对象。该任务既需要全局语义感知，也需要对细微局部证据的精确检查，因为语义相似的物体可能仅在小块可疑区域上存在差异。为应对这一挑战，我们提出 LocalAgent，一个协作式智能体框架，它整合了通用 MLLM 与轻量级专家验证器的互补优势。MLLM 首先进行全局推理以识别可疑局部区域，随后将这些区域委托给局部证据验证器（LEV）工具包进行细粒度外观与几何匹配。LEV 包括局部外观一致性（LAC），用于估计光照和颜色变化下的外观相似度，以及局部几何对应（LGC），用于估计视角变化下的空间对应关系。LEV 返回结构化标量证据，由 MLLM 整合以做出最终决策。我们进一步引入辅助上限强化微调（RFT）策略，其中答案正确性主导辅助工具使用和格式信号，使策略能够学习何时需要验证。实验表明，LocalAgent 相比最强的 CoT-RFT 基线平均准确率提升 4.9%，同时仅在 12.13% 的样本上调用验证器，并保留了底层 MLLM 的通用多模态能力。开源仓库见 https://github.com/Firefly-zoo/LocalAgent-main。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出 LocalAgent 协作式智能体框架，由 MLLM 全局定位可疑区域并交由局部外观与几何验证器返回标量证据，配合辅助上限强化微调，平均准确率较最强 CoT-RFT 基线提升 4.9% 且仅对 12.13% 样本调用验证器。
why_it_matters: 匹配 LLM：large language model, language model
匹配 MLLM / VLM：multimodal large language model
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Transformers as Generic Deep Neural Networks: Exact Compilation, the Cost of Removing Activation-Activation Products, and Multi-Agent Attention Clustering
papers.abstract_en: Transformers are deployed as a special model class. Neural processing units (NPU) add dedicated operators for attention and normalization, and quantization relies on Transformer-specific algorithms. We show the computation does not force this. Every Transformer block, with attention, LayerNorm and a GELU MLP, compiles exactly into a generic deep neural network built from fixed affine maps, routing and the square, sigmoid and inverse square root, plus GELU or its sigmoid approximation. Without activation-activation products, every transform-wise compilation adds at least $N^2$ scalar nonlinear evaluations per head for dense scores. Keeping that one operation type removes this cost; its elementwise form, present on every surveyed NPU, suffices with the sigmoid and inverse square root. For top-$k$ attention with exchangeable tail scores, we prove that exact or conditional-mean tail mass gives an unbiased, minimum-mean-square-error estimate of the attention distribution, while tail drop is conditionally biased. When queries or agents cluster, centroids choose the keys first, reducing the number of computed scores from $N^2$ to $Nk$ per head. On DeiT-Tiny, MambaIRv2-Light and Pythia-70M the compiled models match their references with all keys, standard post-training quantization applies, and the exact tail-mass estimate beats tail dropping with half as many keys on DeiT-Tiny and, for $k\le8$, on Pythia-70M.
papers.abstract_zh: Transformer 被部署为一个特殊的模型类别。神经处理单元（NPU）为注意力和归一化添加了专用算子，而量化依赖 Transformer 专用算法。我们表明，其计算并不必然如此。每个包含注意力、LayerNorm 和 GELU MLP 的 Transformer 块，都能精确编译为由固定仿射映射、路由以及平方、sigmoid 和逆平方根，外加 GELU 或其 sigmoid 近似构成的通用深度神经网络。在没有激活-激活乘积的情况下，对于稠密分数，每个按变换方式的编译在每个头上至少增加 $N^2$ 次标量非线性求值。保留这一种操作类型即可消除该开销；其逐元素形式存在于所有调研的 NPU 上，配合 sigmoid 和逆平方根即已足够。对于尾部分数可交换的 top-$k$ 注意力，我们证明精确或条件均值尾部质量能给出注意力分布的无偏、最小均方误差估计，而尾部丢弃则是有条件有偏的。当查询或智能体聚类时，质心首先选择键，将每个头计算的分数数量从 $N^2$ 减少到 $Nk$。在 DeiT-Tiny、MambaIRv2-Light 和 Pythia-70M 上，编译后的模型在使用全部键时与其参考模型匹配，标准训练后量化适用，且精确尾部质量估计在 DeiT-Tiny 上以一半的键数、在 Pythia-70M 上对于 $k\le8$ 时优于尾部丢弃。
papers.tldr_zh: 证明 Transformer 块可精确编译为通用深度神经网络，指出去除激活-激活乘积的 $N^2$ 开销，并证明 top-$k$ 注意力中精确尾部质量估计无偏且优于尾部丢弃。
why_it_matters: 匹配 预训练 / 后训练：post-training
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Zero-Shot Domain Generalization via Domain Prompt Learning
papers.abstract_en: Domain generalization (DG) aims to improve the generalization of the model to any unseen domains. Targeting this goal, existing DG methods mainly focus on learning domain-invariant features or prompts from the given source domains. However, these methods rely on source-domain data, and collecting and annotating large-scale single- or multi-source datasets is often infeasible, limiting the practical applicability of DG. To tackle this challenge, we propose {\underline{Do}}main \underline{P}rompt Learning (DoP), a method built on a large vision-language model (e.g., CLIP) for zero-shot domain generalization, which recognizes unseen classes in unseen target domains without access to source-domain data. DoP essentially learns the target domain knowledge via prompt both in text and visual modalities to overcome the domain shift in text-visual modalities under the test-time adaptation formulation. Specifically, DoP first takes text domain learning (TDL) to simulate various distribution shifts by learning diverse style tokens implicitly in the text space with inter-style diversity loss and intra-style consistency loss. Subsequently, DoP employs visual domain learning (VDL) to further refine the target-domain-relevant style token generated by TDL by making use of the test visual data with self-supervised learning. Extensive experiments on popular DG benchmark datasets (e.g., PACS, VLCS, OfficeHome, and DomainNet) and ImageNet show that our DoP consistently outperforms the state-of-the-art DG approaches. Codes are available at: https://github.com/shiming-chen/DoP.
papers.abstract_zh: 领域泛化（DG）旨在提升模型对任意未见领域的泛化能力。为此，现有 DG 方法主要致力于从给定源领域学习领域不变特征或提示。然而，这些方法依赖源领域数据，而收集和标注大规模单源或多源数据集往往不可行，限制了 DG 的实际适用性。为应对这一挑战，我们提出领域提示学习（DoP），一种基于大型视觉-语言模型（如 CLIP）的零样本领域泛化方法，可在无法访问源领域数据的情况下识别未见目标领域中的未见类别。DoP 本质上在测试时自适应框架下，通过文本和视觉两种模态的提示学习目标领域知识，以克服文本-视觉模态间的领域偏移。具体而言，DoP 首先采用文本领域学习（TDL），通过在文本空间中隐式学习多样风格 token，并配合风格间多样性损失和风格内一致性损失，模拟各种分布偏移。随后，DoP 采用视觉领域学习（VDL），利用测试视觉数据通过自监督学习进一步精炼 TDL 生成的目标领域相关风格 token。在常用 DG 基准数据集（如 PACS、VLCS、OfficeHome 和 DomainNet）以及 ImageNet 上的大量实验表明，我们的 DoP 持续优于最先进的 DG 方法。代码见：https://github.com/shiming-chen/DoP。
papers.tldr_zh: DoP 基于 CLIP 在测试时通过文本与视觉模态的领域提示学习模拟并适应分布偏移，在无源数据条件下实现零样本领域泛化。
evidence: 实验或理论证据信号：state-of-the-art, extensive experiment
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: The Instruction Tax on Factual Recall: Base Models Can Beat Their Instruction-Tuned Counterparts
papers.abstract_en: We present our solution to the AKBC LM-KBC 2026 Shared Task, where we achieved a score of 0.6836 on the official leaderboard, more than double the baseline of 0.2964. This task requires generating all possible objects for subject-relation pairs using a language model with up to 32 billion parameters, with no retrieval or fine-tuning involved. We show that the prompting methodology is as important as the model architecture: while the instruction-tuned model version achieves 0.5681 with its chat interface, the base model achieves 0.6836 when prompted using text completion. Thus, instruction tuning decreases factual recall; we refer to this effect as the instruction tax, which is caused by the model's weights rather than the prompting method. Our final solution is fairly straightforward: we prompt the base model with some examples from the training data, generate 64--256 outputs, and retain only the repeated ones. Two specialized methods are then applied for each relation: one improves the recall of large answer sets, and the other verifies a person's vitality before predicting their place of death.
papers.abstract_zh: 我们展示了对 AKBC LM-KBC 2026 共享任务的解决方案，在官方排行榜上取得 0.6836 的分数，超过 0.2964 基线两倍以上。该任务要求使用参数量最多 320 亿的语言模型为 subject-relation 对生成所有可能的对象，不涉及检索或微调。我们表明，提示方法与模型架构同样重要：指令微调模型版本在其聊天界面下取得 0.5681，而基座模型在使用文本补全提示时取得 0.6836。因此，指令微调降低了事实召回；我们将这一效应称为指令税，它由模型权重而非提示方法导致。我们的最终方案相当直接：用训练数据中的一些示例提示基座模型，生成 64--256 个输出，仅保留重复出现的输出。随后对每种关系应用两种专门方法：一种提升大答案集的召回，另一种在预测人物死亡地点前验证其是否在世。
papers.tldr_zh: 在 AKBC LM-KBC 2026 任务中，用文本补全提示基座模型并保留重复输出，取得 0.6836 分（基线 0.2964），并指出指令微调会降低事实召回，称为指令税。
why_it_matters: 匹配 预训练 / 后训练：instruction tuning
匹配 模型架构：model architecture
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: GaP-MoE : Explicit Expert Specialization in Mixture-of-Experts via Orthogonal Gradient Accumulation and Projection
papers.abstract_en: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (SMoE) models improve scalability by routing input tokens to only a subset of expert networks, but they often suffer from representation collapse, in which multiple experts converge toward similar functions and lose their intended diversity. Prior work has addressed this limitation either by improving router architectures or by introducing auxiliary loss terms that implicitly penalize similarity among experts. However, router-based approaches remain vulnerable to routing collapses, and loss-based approaches can conflict with the task's original objective during optimization. In this work, we propose GaP-MoE (Gradient Accumulation and Projection in MoE), which induces expert specialization by directly manipulating expert output gradients rather than modifying the loss function. At each training step, GaP-MoE stochastically selects one of the $TopK$ routed experts as a leader based on normalized routing scores, and projects the gradients of the remaining follower experts onto the orthogonal complement of the subspace spanned by the leader's recent gradients. This removes directional overlap between expert gradients without altering the task loss, allowing specialization to emerge as a direct consequence of the optimization dynamics rather than an externally imposed constraint. We evaluate GaP-MoE in both fine-tuning settings (BERT-based, on GLUE) and from-scratch pretraining settings (GPT-2-based, on WikiText-103, enwik8, and text8), and further confirm its compatibility as a drop-in module for existing SMoE architectures. Experimental results show that GaP-MoE achieves performance comparable to or better than standard SMoE.
papers.abstract_zh: 稀疏混合专家（SMoE）模型通过将输入 token 路由到仅一部分专家网络来提升可扩展性，但它们常遭受表示坍缩，即多个专家收敛到相似功能并失去预期的多样性。先前工作通过改进路由器架构或引入隐式惩罚专家间相似性的辅助损失项来解决这一局限。然而，基于路由器的方法仍易受路由坍缩影响，而基于损失的方法在优化过程中可能与任务原始目标冲突。在本工作中，我们提出 GaP-MoE（MoE 中的梯度累积与投影），它通过直接操纵专家输出梯度而非修改损失函数来诱导专家专业化。在每个训练步骤中，GaP-MoE 根据归一化路由分数随机选择 $TopK$ 个被路由专家之一作为领导者，并将其余跟随专家的梯度投影到领导者近期梯度所张成子空间的正交补上。这在改变任务损失的情况下消除了专家梯度之间的方向重叠，使专业化作为优化动态的直接结果而非外部施加的约束而涌现。我们在微调设置（基于 BERT，在 GLUE 上）和从头预训练设置（基于 GPT-2，在 WikiText-103、enwik8 和 text8 上）中评估 GaP-MoE，并进一步确认其作为现有 SMoE 架构即插即用模块的兼容性。实验结果表明，GaP-MoE 取得与标准 SMoE 相当或更好的性能。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出 GaP-MoE，通过将跟随专家梯度投影到领导者专家近期梯度的正交补来消除方向重叠，在不改任务损失的情况下诱导专家专业化，在微调与从头预训练设置中性能与标准 SMoE 相当或更优。
why_it_matters: 匹配 预训练 / 后训练：pretraining
limitations: 当前仅检查标题和摘要，尚未核验正文、实验细节与可复现性。

papers.title: Parallel Thinking for Large Language Model with Path Diversity
papers.abstract_en: Parallel thinking has emerged as a promising paradigm for enhancing the reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) by exploring multiple reasoning paths simultaneously. However, we identify that parallel thinking via Reinforcement Learning (RL) typically suffers from the mode collapse of reasoning paths, where parallel thinking trajectories degenerate into similar ones. This homogeneity undermines the fundamental motivation of parallel thinking, that is, maintaining multiple hypotheses concurrently to prevent premature loss into a suboptimal solution. In this paper, we propose Diverse Parallel Thinking (DPT), a simple yet effective RL approach for parallel thinking designed to encourage path diversity. DPT rewards the model to develop distinct reasoning strategies by penalizing the prefix similarity of parallel thinking paths, thereby enhancing a more comprehensive exploration of the reasoning space. We conduct various experiments and analyses across multiple reasoning benchmarks to demonstrate the effectiveness of DPT. Results show that DPT successfully outperforms previous parallel thinking methods, achieving state-of-the-art performance over baselines. We validate path diversity as a key element to improve parallel thinking. Our code is available at https://github.com/JiaruQian/DPT.
papers.abstract_zh: 并行思考已成为增强大语言模型（LLM）推理能力的一种有前景的范式，它通过同时探索多条推理路径来实现。然而，我们发现基于强化学习（RL）的并行思考通常遭受推理路径的模式坍缩，即并行思考轨迹退化为相似轨迹。这种同质性削弱了并行思考的根本动机，即同时维持多个假设以防止过早陷入次优解。本文提出多样化并行思考（DPT），一种简单而有效的并行思考 RL 方法，旨在鼓励路径多样性。DPT 通过惩罚并行思考路径的前缀相似度来奖励模型发展不同的推理策略，从而增强对推理空间更全面的探索。我们在多个推理基准上进行了多种实验和分析，以证明 DPT 的有效性。结果表明，DPT 成功优于先前的并行思考方法，在基线上取得最先进性能。我们验证了路径多样性是改进并行思考的关键要素。代码见 https://github.com/JiaruQian/DPT。
papers.tldr_zh: DPT 通过惩罚并行思考路径的前缀相似度来鼓励路径多样性，缓解 RL 并行思考中的模式坍缩并在推理基准上取得最优性能。
why_it_matters: 匹配 LLM：large language model, language model
evidence: 开放资源信号：code is available

papers.title: A Transformer-based Approach for Real-time Multi-agent Path Planning with Varying Initial/Final Conditions
papers.abstract_en: We address the problem of real-time multi-agent path planning under prescribed initial and final configurations, formulated as a high-dimensional optimal control problem subject to inter-agent collision avoidance and obstacle constraints. Classical solvers based on the Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation or Pontryagin's maximum principle (PMP) become computationally intractable as the number of agents grows, due to the curse of dimensionality and the non-convexity introduced by interaction constraints. We propose OCFormer, a transformer-based neural network that parameterizes the inverse of a coordinate transformation mapping a simple, analytically tractable latent space, in which agents evolve independently under a decoupled Hamiltonian, to the physical space of the coupled, interacting system. The model is trained by minimizing a physics-informed loss comprising the Hamiltonian ODE residual from the PMP and a boundary matching term, without requiring pre-computed trajectory data. The self-attention mechanism endows OCFormer with permutation equivariance over agents, a structural symmetry that prior symplectic network approaches do not natively enforce. When trained on a distribution of boundary conditions, the amortized OCFormer produces near-optimal trajectories for unseen initial and final configurations in a single forward pass ($\sim$220ms), enabling real-time inference without retraining. We further introduce a lightweight transfer learning framework that adapts a pretrained OCFormer to out-of-distribution perturbations in seconds via L-BFGS fine-tuning. Numerical experiments on two- and three-dimensional multi-agent navigation with up to 128 agents demonstrate the scalability and efficiency of the proposed approach.
papers.abstract_zh: 我们研究在给定初始与终止构型下的实时多智能体路径规划问题，将其建模为受智能体间避碰与障碍约束的高维最优控制问题。基于 Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman 方程或 Pontryagin 极大值原理（PMP）的经典求解器，随着智能体数量增长，由于维数灾难以及交互约束引入的非凸性，在计算上变得不可行。我们提出 OCFormer，一种基于 Transformer 的神经网络，它参数化一个坐标变换的逆映射：该变换将简单、可解析处理的潜空间（其中智能体在解耦哈密顿量下独立演化）映射到耦合、交互系统的物理空间。该模型通过最小化一个物理信息损失进行训练，该损失由来自 PMP 的哈密顿 ODE 残差与边界匹配项组成，无需预先计算的轨迹数据。自注意力机制赋予 OCFormer 对智能体的置换等变性，这是一种先前的辛网络方法未原生强制施加的结构对称性。在边界条件分布上训练后，摊销后的 OCFormer 可在单次前向传播（约 220ms）中为未见过的初始与终止构型生成近最优轨迹，从而实现无需重新训练的实时推理。我们进一步引入一个轻量级迁移学习框架，通过 L-BFGS 微调在数秒内将预训练的 OCFormer 适配到分布外扰动。在最多 128 个智能体的二维与三维多智能体导航上的数值实验证明了所提方法的可扩展性与效率。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出基于 Transformer 的 OCFormer，通过参数化从解耦潜空间到交互物理空间的坐标变换逆映射，以物理信息损失无监督训练，单次前向传播约 220ms 即可为未见边界条件生成近最优多智能体轨迹，并可用 L-BFGS 快速迁移。

papers.title: ULME: Predictive Coupling for Mutually Reinforcing Embedding and Language Modeling
papers.abstract_en: Text embedding and text generation are two of the most useful capabilities of modern large language models, yet they are typically provided by separate specialized models (an embedder and a generator) trained with incompatible objectives and deployed side by side in retrieval-augmented generation and agent systems. Recent unified embedding-generation models such as GritLM share parameters between the two capabilities, but they either switch attention regimes between modes or optimize embedding and language modeling as parallel objectives that never supervise each other. We argue that these designs are only partially unified: the two capabilities coexist on the same weights, but do not shape each other. We propose ULME, a post-training framework that unifies embedding and language modeling on a causal decoder-only LLM through predictive coupling. ULME inserts a chain of learnable slots between the query and the answer, reads a semantic embedding and a reasoning embedding from two designated slots, and trains three objectives on a shared causal backbone: a contrastive loss anchoring the semantic slot to document representations, a language-modeling loss supervising answer generation, and a stop-gradient predictive loss that aligns the reasoning slot with a pooled summary of the answer, so that generation actively shapes what the embedding encodes. Across two model families (Qwen2.5, Qwen3) and eight scales spanning 0.5B-8B parameters, a single ULME checkpoint improves MTEB by 3.3-4.1 points over the strongest open-source baseline, tightens BRIGHT and AdvBench-IR simultaneously, and remains on par with a generation-only fine-tune on standard accuracy benchmarks (MMLU, GSM8K, MMLU-Pro, HumanEval), demonstrating that genuine unification yields mutually reinforcing rather than merely coexisting capabilities.

papers.title: Reasoning-Search-Augmented LLMs: An Operational Taxonomy, Benchmark Analysis and Controlled Evidence Synthesis
papers.abstract_en: Large language models (LLMs) demonstrate impressive emergent reasoning capabilities, yet they remain constrained by fixed model parameters and finite context windows. Even when augmented with static retrieval, they can produce statements that are unsupported by, or even contradictory to, retrieved evidence. This leads to hallucinations, difficulty incorporating up-to-date information, and failures to correctly interpret or reconcile sources. Recent work addresses these limitations by tightly coupling step-by-step reasoning with interactive search, treating retrieval as an action within an iterative agentic loop rather than a one-shot preprocessing step. This study reviews frameworks that implement such reasoning-search loops by interleaving planning, querying, retrieval, integration, verification, and stopping. We analyze these systems through four architectural axes: retrieval coupling, controller design, knowledge source, and grounding strictness. We separately treat the learning signal as a cross-cutting dimension because prompting, supervision, preference optimization, and reinforcement learning can instantiate the same architecture while producing materially different search, stopping, and grounding behavior. We further distinguish benchmark difficulty from RSA-loop demand and synthesize controlled within-study ablations and quality-cost deltas, avoiding invalid pooling across heterogeneous model backbones, retrievers, corpora, and evaluation protocols. Our goal is to clarify the landscape of reasoning-search-augmented LLMs and outline a unified perspective on the design choices shaping future research.

papers.title: Semantic Observability for Autonomous Systems Diagnostics
papers.abstract_en: Modern distributed microservice deployments generate massive volumes of heterogeneous, multi-format observability logs across physically and logically partitioned infrastructure. Isolating root causes during cascading failures remains an arduous task for Site Reliability Engineers (SREs), bottlenecked by manual keyword filtering and disjointed temporal correlation across monitoring dashboards. We introduce Semantic Observability, an autonomous multi-agent framework that unifies disparate log streams into a dynamic, queryable Property Graph Database. By modeling physical infrastructure topologies, logical software dependencies, and chronological event sequences as attributed nodes and directed relations, it bridges the semantic gap inherent in flat, unstructured log repositories. Building on this unified substrate, we deploy a stateful multi-agent system orchestrated through Directed Cyclic Graphs (DCGs). The system autonomously navigates the topology, applying causal graph algorithms and temporal back-traversal to isolate the precise blast radius of anomalies. The pruned subgraph is then interpreted by a Large Language Model (LLM) reasoning engine to generate contextualized, code-level Root Cause Analyses (RCA) and actionable remediations. This paper establishes the foundational system architecture, formal relational ontology, and multi-agent control loops of Semantic Observability. We show conceptually how the framework eliminates ambient telemetry noise, reduces Mean Time to Resolution (MTTR), compresses LLM token consumption, and prevents structural hallucinations. We also specify an open-source validation framework on standard benchmarks (LogHub and Train-Ticket), laying the groundwork for a forthcoming companion paper on exhaustive quantitative evaluation and production benchmarking.

papers.title: MoG-VLM: Efficient Video Anomaly Detection through Motion-Guided Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have shown strong potential for video anomaly detection, but dense frame-level inference makes them impractical for real-time deployment. Existing acceleration commonly relies on uniform sampling, which ignores content dynamics and can either waste computation on static segments or miss localized anomalies. We propose MoG-VLM a motion-adaptive anomaly detection framework that leverages motion purely as a lightweight control signal to decide when VLM inference is necessary. To this end, we introduce Temporal Gradient Magnitude (TGM) which performs content-aware sampling to concentrate computation on informative regions while avoiding redundant processing. We further introduce a hierarchical dual-stream design in which dense multi-frame VLM reasoning is activated only around frames with elevated anomaly likelihood, via anchor-triggered context-window expansion with early termination. A fusion module then reconciles these instantaneous semantic cues with temporal action dynamics. Across four benchmarks, our method achieves 91.91%, 84.30%, 87.88%, and 78.96% AUC-ROC on XD-Violence, UCF-Crime, MSAD, and ShanghaiTech, respectively, establishing new state of the art on three benchmarks under the zero-shot, training-free setting. On XD-Violence, we improve over the previous best result by +0.57% while delivering a 1.31x inference speedup. These results demonstrate that content-aware allocation of VLM capacity, processing fewer frames more intelligently rather than all frames uniformly, is a more effective axis of progress than uniformly densifying VLM inference across frames. Code is available on GitHub: https://github.com/kdawoud91/MoG-VLM.

papers.title: Gaze2HOI: Gaze-Aware Intention Disambiguation for Egocentric Hand-Object Interaction Forecasting
papers.abstract_en: Anticipating how users will interact with their surroundings is essential for proactive systems that provide timely assistance in AR, VR, and embodied applications. Prior work typically forecasts hand-object interactions directly from historical observations, leaving intention and contact geometry implicit. However, similar observation histories can precede semantically or geometrically distinct futures. Inspired by behavioral evidence that gaze can provide early cues for underlying intention, we propose Gaze2HOI, a gaze-aware framework that formulates hand-object interaction forecasting as a hierarchical problem comprising intention inference, contact grounding, and coupled hand-object motion generation. Specifically, Gaze2HOI first weights gaze cues by fixation strength and recency, and uses them to modulate the visual representations of a vision-language model (VLM) through Temporal Gaze Saliency Modulation (TGSM), thereby reducing semantic ambiguity in intention inference. Subsequently, an Anticipatory Contact Grounding (ACG) module maps these structured intentions into explicit contact, support, and placement fields, effectively mitigating geometric ambiguity. Driven by these explicit conditions, a diffusion-based model jointly generates the 6-DoF object trajectories and future articulated motion of both hands. To evaluate Gaze2HOI, we further introduce EgoAIM, a phase-aware benchmark that organizes egocentric hand-object interactions into four phases defined by evolving hand-object relations and provides fine-grained intention annotations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Gaze2HOI achieves state-of-the-art performance in both intention inference and motion forecasting, even approaching oracle-level end-to-end performance in specific interaction phases. Project page: https://gaze2hoi.github.io/.

papers.title: Making MLLM Latents Matter: Factor-Aware Predictive Learning for Cinematic Video Generation
papers.abstract_en: Cinematic video generation requires both temporal inference from limited inputs (i.e., sparse rather than frame-by-frame guidance) and factor-aware control of character, scene, action, and camera. Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) offer useful priors for both capabilities, but their representations are not automatically actionable for video generation: a Video Diffusion Transformer (DiT) may bypass them through native conditioning pathways, and using them does not ensure either factor-aware control or generation-compatible temporal prediction. We propose Factor-Aware Predictive Learning (FAPL), which establishes effective MLLM latent use as a shared prerequisite and then targets the two capabilities with complementary learning signals. First, latent-only generator grounding trains the DiT with a frozen MLLM and connector, strengthening the DiT's use of MLLM latents for generation. Second, for factor-aware control, paired videos specify a target-factor change and non-target preservation, and factor-span replacement trains the DiT to realize this relationship in its output. Third, for temporal inference, text-only and text-plus-complete-video observations share a video target, and the trained DiT is then frozen while the MLLM and connector are optimized through it. This final stage trains limited-input representations for generation while retaining complete-observation reconstruction as a complementary training mode. Extensive experiments demonstrate our consistently better performance on three cinematic video generation tasks (i.e., sparse-to-video, factor-aware editing, and multi-shot generation) over baselines and validate FAPL's contributions to MLLM feature use, temporal control, and factor coordination.

papers.title: Attention-based Classification for Indirect Prompt Injection
papers.abstract_en: Indirect prompt injection (IPI) attacks, in which adversarial instructions are embedded in external data processed by a language model, pose a significant threat to the integrity of deployed LLM agents. Attention Tracker (Hung et al., 2025) is a recently proposed white-box detection method that identifies prompt injection attacks by monitoring how a model's attention is distributed between user task tokens and data tokens, claiming dataset-agnostic detection via a scalar focus score threshold. In this paper, we provide the first evaluation of Attention Tracker in a realistic agentic IPI setting using the AgentDojo benchmark, finding that the dataset agnosticism claim does not hold. We find that in agentic environments, long structured tool outputs subvert the fundamental assumptions Attention Tracker makes about attention that the method depends on and produces near-chance detection on AgentDojo across most model families. We propose AttnDA, an extension replacing the scalar threshold with a Fisher Linear Discriminant Analysis classifier over the per-head focus score vector, and evaluate both methods in a cross-dataset setting spanning four benchmarks. AttnDA improves detection performance across agentic and tool-integrated benchmarks, though transfer to AgentDojo remains challenging regardless of classifier choice. A covariance ablation further shows that removing inter-head correlation structure substantially contributes to performance, with complex covariance assumptions causing significant degradation on cross-domain data. These results indicate that the attentional distraction signal underlying focus-score-based detection does not transfer reliably to agentic environments, and that learned linear classifiers over head-level attention features offer improved detection performance, provided training data from the target deployment domain is available.

papers.title: Africa-Papers: A 10-Billion-Token Multi-Domain Academic Corpus for African Foundation Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Large Language Models (LLMs) depend fundamentally on the diversity, depth, and factual rigor of their pre-training corpora. However, contemporary foundational pre-training datasets (such as The Pile, S2ORC, and Dolma) exhibit a severe structural omission: African scientific, medical, legal, and agricultural scholarship constitutes less than 0.5% of global pre-training tokens. Consequently, state-of-the-art models suffer from systematic failure modes when reasoning about tropical epidemiology, localized smallholder agro-ecologies, regional economic governance, and indigenous linguistic structures. To resolve this representation deficit and advance African intellectual sovereignty in artificial intelligence, we introduce Africa-Papers, the largest curated multi-domain Pan-African academic pre-training corpus to date. Comprising over 844,807 full-text papers spanning 10.15 billion tokens across 879 Parquet shards, Africa-Papers unifies four primary scientific streams: (1) continental peer-reviewed journals indexed in DOAJ across 31 African nations, (2) the CGIAR CGSpace agricultural repository, (3) African-authored and African-focused STEM/AI preprints on arXiv, and (4) open-access international publications by scholars affiliated with African institutions indexed via OpenAlex. The entire corpus is processed into layout-aware, clean Markdown preserving section hierarchies, mathematical equations, and tabular data, accompanied by exact BPE token counts and a standardized 8-domain taxonomy. We release Africa-Papers openly on the Hugging Face Hub under the AfriSpeech organization to accelerate continual pre-training and domain evaluation for foundation models globally.

papers.title: RECAP: Looking Once Is Not Enough for Vision-Language Reasoning
papers.abstract_en: Long chain-of-thought reasoning improves vision-language models (VLMs), but it also exposes a temporal grounding failure: as generation unfolds, models may drift from image evidence while reinforcement learning still provides only a final-answer reward. We study this gap through visual revisit, a temporally localized reactivation of image evidence during reasoning. Across three VLM backbones, revisit peaks are predictive of correctness and causally linked to performance: masking them degrades accuracy more than masking non-peaks, while injecting revisit-like peaks into failed rollouts partially restores correct answers. Control analyses show that this signal is not explained by raw attention strength, uncertainty, logit margin, or hidden-state norm. We propose RECAP, a GRPO-compatible training method that turns detached revisit traces into a credit-assignment signal. RECAP uses revisit-conditioned advantage estimation, dynamic discounting, and gated value prediction to propagate final rewards through visually important reasoning steps, without extra rewards, additional rollouts, or inference-time changes. Across Qwen2.5-VL-7B, InternVL3-8B, and LLaVA-OV-7B, RECAP consistently improves over GRPO and VPPO, yielding $+6.1$--$+6.5$ HallusionBench gains over the SFT base while preserving reasoning and text-only performance. Results on larger LoRA-tuned models, Chinese zero-shot benchmarks, visual perturbations, and human evaluation further demonstrate robust improvements in image-grounded reasoning.

papers.title: LLMSeg: Training-Free Text-Prompted Image Segmentation with B-Splines
papers.abstract_en: Promptable segmentation models such as SAM 3 achieve remarkable open-vocabulary performance but require dedicated architectures, large-scale annotation engines, and task-specific training. We ask a different question: can a general-purpose multimodal large language model (MLLM) segment images directly, without an added segmentation head, mask decoder, or training? We present LLMSeg, a training-free pipeline that turns a vision-capable LLM into a text-prompted image segmenter. LLMSeg decomposes segmentation into three LLM-driven stages. First, detect localizes all instances matching a free-form text query and describes their coarse morphology. Next, segment traces each instance using closed periodic B-splines confined to its detected box. These splines define an outer boundary and optional hole loops. Finally, refine iteratively proposes focus boxes around residual errors and retraces confined splines. The process ends when the mask stabilizes or the pass budget is exhausted. The output is a binary mask with inspectable intermediate geometry. We evaluate LLMSeg across ten referring and reasoning segmentation splits (ReasonSeg and RefCOCO/+/g). We also evaluate open-vocabulary instance segmentation (LVIS, COCO, and SA-Co), semantic segmentation, and zero-shot detection (ODinW13 and RF-100VL). With an off-the-shelf Gemini-3.7-Flash backend, LLMSeg is competitive with and often surpasses the specialist SAM 3 model on identical items. It reaches 71.5 cIoU on ReasonSeg val without additional segmentation-specific training. Backend model updates can improve accuracy without retraining the pipeline. The code is available at https://abdullahamdi.com/llmseg .

papers.title: Don't Skip the Baseline: A Controlled Comparison of Dynamic Expert Skipping in MoEs
papers.abstract_en: A growing body of work proposes dynamic expert-skipping methods for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models that adjust the number of experts activated per token during inference, aiming to preserve model quality while further reducing the number of active parameters. These methods have added calibrated importance scores, inter-expert similarity metrics, or learned per-token allocators in order to identify experts to skip. However, different calibration regimes, different reductions in the effective number of experts, and evaluation suites make comparisons difficult. We classify four representative prior methods into a unified taxonomy and benchmark them against a natural, simple baseline: statically reducing the number of experts $k$ (i.e., same reduced $k$ across all layers and tokens). We provide a fair comparison of these methods at matched expert-compute budget, on two modern MoEs (Gemma4-26B-A4B and Qwen3-30B-A3B) in a text-only setting and a contemporary vision-language model (Qwen3-VL) in a multimodal setting. Surprisingly, we find that the simple baseline is hard to outperform consistently across models, modalities, benchmarks, and calibration settings. The methods we benchmark often underperform the baseline and achieved gains, when present, are minor. We further find that the effective $k$ achieved (or optimized for) in calibration can diverge from the effective $k$ in testing, resulting in over- or under-estimating the compute at inference time. Based on these findings, we recommend a calibration-free per-modality static $k$ reduction and validate this on a held-out model and modality. We further argue that a static control at matched measured compute is the baseline any dynamic skipping method must beat.

papers.title: SmolVLA-MoE: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts for Efficient Multi-Task Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract_en: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown promising results in multi-task robotic manipulation by leveraging visual and language understanding for action generation. However, existing lightweight VLA models employ a single dense action expert to handle all tasks, which limits their multi-task capability under constrained computational budgets. To address this issue, we propose SmolVLA-MoE, a novel framework that introduces sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) into the FFN layers of the action expert in VLA models. SmolVLA-MoE replaces dense FFN layers with multiple parallel expert FFNs and a token-level router, enabling each token to adaptively select the most suitable expert for action generation. We further introduce a shared expert with a tunable weight parameter to balance the inheritance of pre-trained capabilities and task-specific expert specialization. Through sparse activation, SmolVLA-MoE activates only a single expert FFN during inference, with a total activated parameter count of approximately 500M including the frozen VLM backbone, while benefiting from approximately 800M total stored parameters. We evaluate our method on four task suites of the LIBERO benchmark. SmolVLA-MoE achieves an average success rate of 84.25%, outperforming SmolVLA (82.75%) and OpenVLA-7B (76.5%), while maintaining comparable inference efficiency. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/dudu435/smolvla-moe.

papers.title: EPIC: Rethinking Trust Regions for Autoregressive LLM Policies via Exact-KL Prefix Importance-Ratio Clipping
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning (RL) based on PPO-style clipping has become an effective approach to improving the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs). However, standard token-level clipping measures policy change only through the conditional probability of the current token, while the prefix conditioning context is itself generated by the policy. This mismatch becomes especially consequential in long-response and off-policy training. We reformulate autoregressive generation as a finite-horizon Markov decision process and derive its performance-difference identity under behavior-policy sampling. The resulting change of measure identifies the cumulative likelihood ratio of the generated prefix as the exact importance weight for each stepwise policy-improvement term. Starting from the monotonic-improvement principle of trust-region policy optimization, we then construct a prefix-level trust region using the exact reverse-KL coordinate $r-1-\log r$, whose behavior-policy expectation equals the corresponding prefix-distribution KL divergence. This yields EPIC, a PPO-style sequence-clipping method that directly regulates prefix-level policy drift without relying on a local quadratic approximation or expert-routing replay. Experiments on off-policy reinforcement learning with a sparse mixture-of-experts language model show that EPIC consistently outperforms standard and sequence-level clipping baselines across mathematical-reasoning benchmarks, while remaining competitive with routing-replay-based alternatives. Code is available at https://github.com/LiChengxi666/EPIC.

papers.title: DocLayout-YOLO: Axis-Attentive Document Layout Detector with Mesh-Guided Synthetic Pretraining
papers.abstract_en: Accurate and efficient document layout analysis is critical for modern document parsing systems. However, although the YOLO framework represents a leading paradigm for the real-time detector, its adaptation to heterogeneous documents remains underexplored. To address this gap, we propose DocLayout-YOLO, a document-specialized real-time detector that integrates diverse synthetic document pretraining and page-axis context modeling. From the data perspective, we introduce MeshLayout-1M, a synthetic pretraining corpus generated by the proposed Mesh-candidate BestFit algorithm, which provides large-scale and diverse document layouts for pretraining and improves adaptation to heterogeneous document scenarios. From the model perspective, we propose Page-Axis Layout Attention (PALA), which captures long-range dependencies along the horizontal and vertical page axes while remaining computationally efficient. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DocLayout-YOLO achieves state-of-the-art performance on four heterogeneous document benchmarks, obtaining 72.4%/75.5%/96.0%/73.1% mAP50:95 on D4LA, M6Doc, HJDataset, and PRIMA-LAD, respectively. Compared with existing real-time detectors, DocLayout-YOLO establishes a superior accuracy-efficiency trade-off in document layout analysis. Code, model, and data are available at https://github.com/opendatalab/DocLayout-YOLO/tree/release-v2.

papers.title: Staged Continual Adaptation of Multimodal Foundation Models for Japanese Financial Documents
papers.abstract_en: Staged post-training of multimodal foundation models chains vision-language alignment, reasoning distillation, and domain tuning, yet how each phase trades capabilities against the others remains under-characterised. Tracking an 8.4B-parameter model from an un-fine-tuned baseline through three training phases on Japanese financial documents (evaluated on five text-input benchmarks), we find the phases interact non-additively: math-only distillation overwrites the financial knowledge acquired earlier even as procedural math skill survives, and the domain phase repairs more than it installs. A skip-phase ablation is best for domain knowledge but forfeits numerical-reasoning gains, so per-phase contributions are not decomposable and the best checkpoint is task-dependent, with implications for checkpoint retention and scheduling rather than added stages.

papers.title: GIFT: Gradient Informed Filtering for Distillation Augmented Reasoning RL
papers.abstract_en: Training large language models for complex reasoning tasks relies on two complementary signals: sparse, outcome-grounded reinforcement learning (RL) for correctness, and dense, token-level distillation for guidance. However, complementarity in supervision does not guarantee compatibility in optimization; imitation-focused distillation can conflict with the outcome-driven RL objective, and existing hybrids lack a principled resolution. We propose \textbf{GIFT} (\textbf{G}radient-\textbf{I}nformed \textbf{F}il\textbf{T}ering for Distillation-Augmented Reasoning RL), a novel method that directly addresses the allocation problem of which teacher updates to apply. GIFT performs a token-level geometric analysis, decomposing the distillation gradient into a component \textbf{parallel} to the RL gradient, which measures first-order conflict and provides a \textbf{safety} filter, and a component \textbf{orthogonal} to it, which quantifies novel directional guidance and provides a measure of \textbf{value}. This decomposition yields a principled scoring rule to rank token-level guidance. We combine this with a progressive \textbf{coverage annealing} schedule that shrinks the budget of tokens receiving distillation, ensuring that the most conflicting updates are discarded first while the most complementary ones are retained at full strength. This facilitates a smooth transition from dense, geometrically-filtered guidance to a pure, outcome-grounded objective at convergence. Extensive experiments on mathematical and logical reasoning benchmarks show that GIFT consistently outperforms strong baselines across multiple model scales, achieving relative gains of up to 9.5\% on difficult mathematical reasoning tasks. Code: https://github.com/lilifree/GIFT

papers.title: UniWALM: Unified World Action Language Model for Embodied Robot Control
papers.abstract_en: Motivated by the human ability to integrate experience across language, perception, and action, we introduce UniWALM, a unified world-action-language model that learns video, action, and language in a single shared representation, where each modality is both a conditioning signal and a supervision target. We ask: can jointly generating language enrich this shared representation, improving manipulation and supporting memory-dependent behavior? Unlike prior approaches that attach a reasoning or vision-language model to a video-action backbone and run them as distinct stages, UniWALM unifies all three modalities inside a single mixture-of-transformers backbone whose per-modality diffusion heads co-denoise synchronously, decoding subtask and textual memory in the same pass as action with no separate planning stage; the generated language is re-consumed on the next step, closing a language-as-memory loop without an external planner or memory bank. To keep the action stream reliable under this richer objective, we further introduce Flow Matching with Correction (FMC), a training objective that teaches recovery from perturbed action trajectories at no inference-time cost. UniWALM consistently improves over same-backbone baselines (e.g., FastWAM) on compositional pick-and-place (MolmoSpaces) and across the memory-dependent subset of RMBench, where it reaches 34.5% without any pretrained language or reasoning model and exceeds Mem-0's keyframe-equipped setup (28.5%) using only a single anchor frame. On a real-world Find-the-Item task, generating textual memory lifts success from 11.1% to 61.1%, while state-of-the-art VLAs stay at or below chance (<=33.3%).

papers.title: How Depth Growth and Looping Shape In-Context Learning in Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Looped and depth-grown language models reuse computations across depth and have attracted interest for their reasoning capabilities. Building on prior suggestive evidence of improved in-context-learning (ICL), we investigate how such reuse favors ICL, including how it shapes the acquisition, retention, and mechanisms of this ability. Our analysis spans pretrained language models up to 3B parameters and controlled tasks. The experiments provide evidence for a shared inductive bias toward learning from context: grown and looped models rely more on information in context and, compared with a full-depth dense reference, acquire ICL earlier in controlled tasks and retain it more strongly when learning fixed associations in the weights is also possible. Tracing attention heads through training reveals that depth growth propagates early induction heads across layers. Ablations show that grown and looped models rely more strongly on induction-ranked heads for both few-shot performance and later-token prediction. Together, these findings provide evidence for a shared inductive bias toward learning from context and suggest that (soft) parameter reuse shapes how this ability develops and which attention mechanisms support it.

papers.title: Future of Time Series Anomaly Detection: From Historical Review to Unified Outlook
papers.abstract_en: Time series anomaly detection (TSAD) is a foundational problem in data mining, aiming to identify observations that deviate significantly from nominal temporal patterns. Driven by escalating data volumes and application complexity, recent research has yielded diverse architectures, including diffusion models, state space models, and large language models (LLMs). However, existing surveys provide limited coverage of these emerging designs and lack a unified treatment of multivariate anomalies, cross-domain unified modeling, metric reliability, and contemporary evaluation challenges. To bridge these gaps, this survey delivers three core contributions: (1) We establish a refined anomaly categorization and a structured taxonomy of paradigms reflecting modern advances, comparing detection mechanisms and charting developmental trajectories across paradigms. (2) We provide an extensive analysis of evaluation methodologies and conduct comprehensive experiments to assess metric fidelity, complemented by an open-source benchmark repository encompassing algorithms, datasets, and evaluation tools. (3) We outline key open challenges, offering forward-looking perspectives on dynamic thresholding, model interpretability, zero-shot transfer, multi-modal alignment, and foundational models for time series. By addressing existing theoretical and empirical limitations, this survey establishes a coherent framework to guide future TSAD research and practical deployments.

papers.title: RoleFlow: Self-Evolving Multi-Role Agentic Collaboration via Structural Adaptation
papers.abstract_en: Large language model (LLM) based multi-agent systems often rely on predefined collaboration structures, limiting their adaptability to evolving task requirements. Although recent approaches enable dynamic orchestration, trajectory-level rewards they apply assign one outcome to each decision, ofen struggling to identify the contributions of individual structural changes. We propose RoleFlow, a self-evolving multi-role agentic system that refines collaboration structures through feedback-driven atomic edits and on-demand role synthesis. To make structural adaptation learnable, we introduce Single-Edit Counterfactual Policy Optimization (SECPO), which evaluates each edit against its no-edit counterpart at the same chain state and assigns targeted credit to edit-specific tokens. Across seven benchmarks spanning four domains, RoleFlow achieves the optimal average performance, surpassing the strongest competitor by 4.7 points. It leads on all three multi-hop QA benchmarks by 3.2-7.5 F1 points and also shows supremacy on mathematical reasoning, web interaction, and code generation. Further analyses demonstrate cross-benchmark transferability, training-data efficiency, and cross-executor generalization.

papers.title: Loop to Look Better: Learning Adaptive Depth for Question-Guided Perception in Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Visual perception should be iterative and task-directed, with representations refined in response to the question and the need for further processing. While Vision-Language Models (VLMs) increasingly support extended reasoning, their visual tokens are still typically acquired in a single, task-agnostic encoder pass. This creates an evidence-acquisition bottleneck: models may reason longer without refining the visual evidence needed to answer the question. We propose LoopLook, a lightweight encoder-side recurrent perception framework that equips pretrained VLMs with adaptive visual depth. LoopLook recurrently revisits a middle-to-late window of the vision encoder, injecting question representations at each loop to guide visual refinement. A learned stopping mechanism adaptively determines the recurrent depth, while a token-wise Mixture-of-Looks (MoL) combines representations from different loops, allowing each visual token to selectively integrate information acquired across recurrent steps. Across four backbones and eight benchmarks, LoopLook consistently improves performance over the baseline, yielding gains of up to 8.6% on MMStar and 8.1% on HallusionBench. Our analysis shows that LoopLook progressively refines visual attention and adaptively allocates depth according to task difficulty. It also better preserves task-relevant visual information under reduced input resolution, while increasing time to first token (TTFT) by only 5.1-6.5%. By bringing recurrence from reasoning back into perception, LoopLook transforms visual perception from a one-shot glimpse into an adaptive process of recurrent refinement.

papers.title: Edit, Don't Imitate: Minimal-Edit On-Policy Distillation for Multimodal Reasoning
papers.abstract_en: Visual mathematical reasoning can fail before reasoning begins: when a vision-language model (VLM) misreads a diagram, subsequent reasoning proceeds from false premises. This perceptual bottleneck is especially pronounced in smaller models, while accurate textual descriptions can substantially narrow the gap to larger models. Because obtaining such descriptions at inference requires additional annotation or model calls, we propose minimal-edit corrective on-policy distillation. Using reference figure descriptions and verified reference solutions as training-only information, a teacher scores incorrect student rollouts under a minimal-edit objective, and only teacher-disfavored tokens contribute to the corrective loss. Correct rollouts receive task-reward reinforcement learning. This preserves on-policy supervision while avoiding full-response imitation. Across model scales, the method requires no descriptions at test time and meets or exceeds the corresponding base model supplied with a reference figure description at inference. It also improves perception-oriented performance, particularly low-level geometric perception, and transfers to external mathematics and perception benchmarks. Because the minimal-edit teacher evaluates corrections rather than generating its own solution, the method remains effective with a frozen same-size teacher, although its gains are smaller than with a larger teacher on most metrics.

papers.title: A Mechanistic Study of Automated Failure Attribution in LLM-based Agentic Systems
papers.abstract_en: Agentic systems have demonstrated strong capabilities on complex tasks by enabling multiple interacting large language model (LLM)-based agents to collaborate and execute subtasks in parallel. However, this collaborative structure introduces new challenges for reliably evaluating and diagnosing system failures, particularly failure attribution: tracing a system's execution to identify the agent step responsible for an incorrect final outcome. Because manually performing this task is time- and labor-intensive, recent work has turned to LLMs as judges to automate the process, referred to as automated failure attribution (AFA). These approaches assume that a sufficiently capable model can infer the failing step directly from an interaction transcript. In practice, however, direct prompting often performs poorly, which motivates follow-up work that explores various ways to improve AFA performance, including alternative prompting strategies and inference-time interventions. In this paper, we examine a more fundamental question: whether this weak behavioral performance reflects a genuine capability limitation. Using linear probes applied to internal activations, we uncover a significant \emph{knows-but-won't-say gap:} models encode sufficient information to attribute a failure correctly but fail to explicitly output the responsible step. Building on this finding, we propose \emph{grafting}, a simple manual intervention that exploits knowledge already encoded in the model to improve AFA performance without requiring ground-truth labels at inference time. Extensive evaluations across multiple LLMs and benchmark settings demonstrate that grafting consistently outperforms direct-prompting approaches, underscoring the potential of leveraging latent model knowledge for more reliable failure attribution. Our code is available at https://github.com/wendyzheng22/mi4afa.

papers.title: DuoCook: An Overcooked-Inspired Benchmark for Visual Planning and Coordination
papers.abstract_en: Coordinating two players in a cooking task requires a vision-language agent to track changing scene states, sequence recipe steps, and allocate shared resources under a time budget. We introduce an Overcooked-inspired benchmark for evaluating these capabilities in Unreal Engine environments constructed using coding agents. A single vision-language model controls both players from top-down visual observations, selecting high-level actions while the engine executes navigation. The benchmark contains 20 maps in five categories. These categories support evaluation of centralized coordination under equipment contention, changing terrain, and handoff dependencies. A prop legend and pot ingredient-count indicators provide explicit visual cues, while grid-based destinations support spatial grounding. The evaluation compares four VLMs on all 20 maps, measuring task score, order completion, delivery precision, action acceptance rate, and model API expenditure. A memory ablation on the same 20 maps examines the effect of a shared, self-authored notebook while retaining six-response action history in both conditions. The strongest evaluated model, \texttt{gpt-6-astra}, achieves 26.2\% mean order completion. Notebook memory has mixed score effects across models, with positive mean differences for Claude and Qwen and negative differences for GPT and Gemini.

papers.title: Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning for Search-State Awareness in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Recent advances in search agents have enabled large language models to tackle complex tasks by retrieving and synthesizing external information. However, existing search agents often lack search-state awareness, i.e., the ability to recognize what information has been obtained and what remains missing, leading to hallucinated reasoning and prematurely terminated search. To address this limitation, we propose Self-Assessment Reinforcement Learning (SARL), a reinforcement learning framework in which models learn to recognize their own search state during training and improve their search behavior accordingly, without requiring additional assessment at test time. SARL achieves this through a dual reward design that captures the corrective effect of each assessment while penalizing excessive reliance on it, jointly encouraging effective and efficient search trajectories. Under this setup, SARL achieves a 24.3% relative improvement over the strongest baseline, with average gains of 35.9% on multi-hop reasoning and 27.9% on deep research benchmarks against the strongest per-benchmark baselines. SARL further surpasses methods built on auxiliary supervision or multi-agent coordination, despite operating as a standalone RL framework with no inference-time scaffolding. Beyond final performance, SARL maintains training stability under extended search horizons, a regime where existing methods consistently degrade, enabling sustained gains as task complexity grows.

papers.title: Temporal Evidence-Parameter Co-Alignment for LLM Reasoning over Temporal Knowledge Graphs
papers.abstract_en: Large Language Models (LLMs) often struggle with temporally grounded reasoning because their static parametric memory is misaligned with the dynamic evolution of real-world knowledge. Although RAG and Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) provide practical ways to enhance LLMs, they remain insufficient for temporal reasoning. Existing retrieval methods typically prioritize semantic relevance while overlooking temporal validity, event order, and evolutionary dependencies, resulting in evidence that is relevant in isolation but temporally fragmented. Meanwhile, conventional PEFT methods usually employ fixed and input-agnostic low-rank updates, making it difficult to capture time-dependent entity semantics and relation drift. To address these limitations, we propose Temporal Evidence-Parameter Co-Alignment (TEPCA), a framework for LLM reasoning over TKGs. TEPCA aligns LLM reasoning with temporal knowledge at both the evidence and parameter levels. At the evidence level, it introduces time-constrained Dynamic Relevance-Guided Path (DRGP) pruning to preserve globally coherent temporal paths, together with Mutual-Information (MI)-based pruning to retain query-informative local facts under temporal constraints. At the parameter level, it integrates Dynamic-Gated LoRA (DG-LoRA), a timestamp-conditioned low-rank adaptation mechanism that dynamically modulates the effective adaptation subspace according to temporal context. This design enables LLMs to better capture fine-grained entity evolution and time-dependent relation semantics while preserving parameter efficiency. Experimental results on two TKG benchmarks demonstrate that TEPCA achieves state-of-the-art performance. Additional evaluations of DG-LoRA on eight commonsense QA datasets further verify its general input-adaptive capacity, scalability across LLM backbones, and interpretability.
